title: The king and his sons (Kern ch. 25)
hook: two princes lead their father to the teaching

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chapter of the Lotus that people chant on its own: Guanyin, who hears the world's cries. Your line: chanted everywhere.

Two young princes want to hear a Buddha teach. Their father, the king, follows a different teaching and isn't interested. So the boys go to their mother first, and her advice is unexpected. Don't sneak off, she says, and don't argue with him. Go to your father and show him something. Let him see, so his mind turns clear. That's chapter twenty-five of the Lotus Sutra, in Kern's numbering: a family story from a past age that runs backward from the way families usually work.
screen: `TWO PRINCES WANT TO GO.` → `THEIR FATHER ISN'T INTERESTED.` → `THEIR MOTHER SAYS: SHOW HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's what the sons do, as the chapter tells it. They rise into the air in front of their father and walk there, sit there, lie down there, as if the sky were a floor. Water and fire stream from their bodies. They grow vast, then small again. The king is astonished, and glad. Who is your teacher, he asks. A Buddha, they answer, teaching the Lotus not far from here. Then I want to see him too, says the king. Notice the direction. Teaching usually flows downhill, from parent to child. Here it runs uphill. The sons don't lecture their father; they show him, and let him ask. They also ask their parents' leave to become monks, and the chapter gives a picture for how rare it is to meet a Buddha: like a turtle adrift on the ocean, surfacing right into the hole of a floating log. Then the whole family goes. The king hears the teaching, and in time he leaves his throne to practice. Here's the chapter's heart. The king tells the Buddha that his two sons have been his good friends; they turned him around. The Buddha agrees: a good friend is a great cause, the one who leads another to see a Buddha and set out on the path. And the ending reveals who these people became. The two sons are the Medicine King, whose story came a few days ago, and his brother. A good friend, in this sutra, can be your own child.
screen: `THE SONS WALK ON THE AIR.` · `WHO IS YOUR TEACHER?` · `A TURTLE AND A FLOATING LOG.` · `MY SONS ARE MY GOOD FRIENDS.` · then, large: `THE SONS LED THE KING.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone younger than you: a child, a niece, a student, the new person at work. Find one thing they know or see better than you do, small or not small at all. For a minute, let it be true that they could lead you somewhere.
The king and his sons. A father led to the teaching by his own children, who showed him instead of arguing. Today's word.
screen: `THE KING AND HIS SONS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the sons led the king. Sometimes the wonder comes first, and the question follows. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, this chapter is taught as a story about the good friend, the person who leads another toward the teaching, and it ties back to the Medicine King chapter, since the two princes are revealed to be the Medicine King and his brother.

chat.meaning: On their mother's advice the sons show their father wonders instead of arguing; he asks who their teacher is and wants to go too.

notes: Chapter paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 25, not quoted. Names left out of the voice (King Subhavyuha, Queen Vimaladatta, sons Vimalagarbha and Vimalanetra in Kern); confirm whether to add them.
'Follows a different teaching': Kern has the king devoted to the brahmans / other doctrines. Phrased neutrally on purpose so no tradition is the foil; confirm.
Wonders paraphrased: walking, sitting and lying in the air, water and fire from their bodies, growing large and small. Confirm against Kern.
The one-eyed turtle and floating log image: confirm it appears in this chapter in Kern's version (it is in Kumarajiva's Chinese). Also the udumbara flower image, not used.
Good friend as 'a great cause': confirm the wording in Kern.
Reveal: the two sons are Bhaishajyaraja (Medicine King) and Bhaishajyasamudgata; confirm for Kern's version. Tied to day 1178.
Kalyanamitra (कल्याणमित्र) as the original-language word: confirm it is the term used in this chapter.
Editor: dropped 'one-eyed' from the turtle image (voice and match pair), since that detail is Kumarajiva's and not confirmed for Kern's version cited here.
